predicate_verbalization.pmt: pmt(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5, arg6, arg7)
predicate_verbalization.p: p(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5)

rule_verbalization.1: If pmt(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5, arg6, arg7) and acc(arg8, arg9, arg1) and acc(arg10, arg11, arg2) and arg3=arg9 and arg4=arg11 then p(arg0, arg9, arg10, arg5, arg6, arg7) holds.
rule_verbalization.2: If p(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5) holds, then it exists arg6 cat(arg0, arg3, arg4, arg5, arg6).
rule_verbalization.3: If cat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4) holds and arg1 belongs to 'Business to Business', then arg4 = 'b2b'.
rule_verbalization.4: If cat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4) holds and arg1 belongs to 'Customer to Business', then arg4 = 'c2b'.
rule_verbalization.5: If cat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4) holds and arg1 belongs to 'Customer to Customer', then arg4 = 'c2c'.
rule_verbalization.6: If cat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4) and P(arg0, arg5, arg6, arg7, arg8, arg9) hold, then frequency(arg5, arg4, count(arg4)) holds.
rule_verbalization.7: If frequency(arg0, arg1, arg2) holds, then maxC(arg0, max(arg2)) holds.
rule_verbalization.8: If maxC(arg0, arg1) and frequency(arg0, arg2, arg1) hold, then maxCategory(arg0, arg2) holds.
rule_verbalization.9: If p(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5) and cat(arg0, arg6, arg7, arg8, arg9) and maxCategory(arg1, arg10) hold and arg9 ≠ arg10, then anomaly(arg0) holds.
